summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled shell and local-service tunneling on installer host
details: When the CLI is run, the agent connects to a relay server (default msclaude.ai) and dispatches WebSocket messages by type into handlers that operate on the installer's host. A `terminal_open` message causes the agent to spawn a bash/powershell PTY via node-pty, and subsequent `terminal_input` messages write remote-sourced bytes into that PTY (dist/... terminal manager: `ptyProcess = pty.spawn(shell, [],...); ptyProcess.write(data)`), giving the remote party the ability to run arbitrary shell commands on the host. Additional message types (`tunnel_request`, `tunnel_ws_open`,...) forward remote traffic to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` / `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` on the installer's machine and stream responses back over the WebSocket, exposing loopback-bound services. Port access is filtered by an allowlist at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json, but the allowlist itself is mutable from the relay via a `proxy_config_update` message. The same dispatcher also exposes handlers for arbitrary file read/write, file upload/download, git commit/push, session listing/deletion, and a scheduler, all reachable from the relay server. The result is a full-host remote-control channel driven by a network-controlled party.
